properties.summary: PostgreSQL source of truth with a Kafka dispatch relay for high-throughput cells.
properties.reason: PostgreSQL remains the acceptance barrier; Kafka carries partition-scoped dispatch work derived from a transactional outbox.
properties.orderingNote: Kafka partition-scoped ordering keyed by assignment/endpoint; PostgreSQL is the acceptance authority.
properties.delayedRetryStrategy: native run_at query with Kafka relay; retry topics/scheduler emulate delay
properties.failureRecovery: loss of Kafka is recoverable by replaying unacknowledged outbox rows; no dual write.

acknowledgementBarrier.reason: Ingest, ledger, payload, and dispatch job commit in one transaction.

durableProtocolV1Acknowledgement.reason: 202 is returned only after the four artifacts are durable.

restartRecovery.reason: PostgreSQL recovers fully; Kafka and the outbox reconcile by replaying unacknowledged rows.

durableIdempotency.reason: Idempotency ledger is durable for the full retry horizon.

leaseFencing.reason: Database-clock leases with fencing tokens prevent stale settlement.

multiReplicaSafe.reason: SKIP LOCKED claims allow multiple API/worker replicas.

replayRedrive.reason: Dead jobs are surfaced and redriven by explicit operator action.

objectStorePayloadBackend.reason: Ciphertext may be stored in an S3-compatible object store; PostgreSQL keeps only the payload-free object locator, checksum, and key metadata. The 202 barrier requires the immutable object PUT plus the PostgreSQL commit. PostgreSQL-byte storage remains the default.

requirements.backupRequirement: PostgreSQL physical or logical backup of the cell database.
